recipes.name: Healthy vegetable rice bowl (Keon-gang-sik yeongyangbap: 건강식 영양밥)
ingredients: 2 ounces kale (60 grams), tough stems removed, washed, drained, and chopped
8 ounces peeled Korean radish (or daikon, turnip), cut into matchsticks
2 large king oyster mushrooms (about 6 ounces), sliced
4 sunny side up eggs (or over easy), optional
gochujang (Korean hot pepper paste) and toasted sesame oil for serving, optional
1 teaspoon sugar (or zero calorie natural sweetener such as Swerve)
instructions: Put the rice in a heavy pot and cover with cold water. Tilt the pot and slowly pour out the water, taking care not to pour out any rice. Swish the wet rice around in the pot with one hand, then fill the pot with cold water again, swish, and drain. Repeat, changing the water each time, until the water runs clear. Drain as much water as possible. The rice will still be wet.
Add 1½ cups water to the rice. Spread the chopped kale evenly over the rice, then add the radish, soybean sprouts, and mushrooms. Cover and let sit for at least 30 minutes to soak the rice.

While the rice soaks, combine the soy sauce, hot pepper flakes, sugar (or Swerve), green onions, garlic, sesame seeds, and toasted sesame oil in a small bowl. Gently mix well with a spoon. Cover and set aside.
Cook the pot over medium high heat for about 7 to 8 minutes.
Uncover and stir the rice, vegetables, and mushrooms with a rice scoop or wooden spoon to make sure nothing is sticking to the bottom of the pot.
Add ¼ cup water and turn over the rice well. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 7 to 8 minutes.
Uncover and carefully taste a little rice; it should be soft. If it is still slightly crunchy, cover and steam for a couple more minutes until fully cooked.
Gently fluff the rice and divide it among 4 individual bowls. Add the optional sunny side up eggs if using. Serve right away with the seasoning sauce, gochujang, and extra toasted sesame oil.
Add seasoning sauce, gochujang, and toasted sesame oil according to your taste. Mix well with a spoon and eat.

ingredient_sections.text: Total time: about 1 hour, including 30 minutes for soaking the rice.
2 ounces kale (60 grams), tough stems removed, washed, drained, and chopped
8 ounces peeled Korean radish (or daikon, turnip), cut into matchsticks
2 large king oyster mushrooms (about 6 ounces), sliced
4 sunny side up eggs (or over easy), optional
gochujang (Korean hot pepper paste) and toasted sesame oil for serving, optional
1 teaspoon sugar (or zero calorie natural sweetener such as Swerve)

DirectionsPrepare the rice:Put the rice in a heavy pot and cover with cold water. Tilt the pot and slowly pour out the water, taking care not to pour out any rice. Swish the wet rice around in the pot with one hand, then fill the pot with cold water again, swish, and drain. Do this a few more times, changing the water each time, until the water runs clear. Drain as much water as you can. The rice will still be wet.Add 1½ cups water to the rice. Place the chopped kale over the rice and spread it evenly. Then add the radish and soy bean sprouts, and mushrooms. Cover and let it sit for at least 30 minutes so that the rice will be soaked.Meanwhile make seasoning sauce:Combine the soy sauce, hot pepper flakes, sugar (or Swerve), green onion, garlic, sesame seeds, and toasted sesame oil in a small bowl. Gently mix them well with a spoon. Cover and set aside.Time to cook:Cook the pot over medium high heat for about 7 to 8 minutes.Uncover and stir the rice, vegetables, and the mushrooms with a rice scoop or a wooden spoon to make sure that none is sticking to the bottom of the pot.Add ¼ cup water and turn over the rice well. Cover and turn down the heat to low. Simmer for 7 to 8 minutes.Uncover the rice and test for doneness. Take a small bite (be careful not to burn your tongue!); the rice should be soft. If it is still slightly crunchy, cover and steam for a couple of minutes more until it is fully cooked. Serve and eat:Gently fluff the rice with a rice scoop and divide the rice into 4 portions and put each portion into individual bowls. Add the sunny side up eggs if used. Serve right away with the seasoning sauce, hot pepper paste (gochujang), and extra sesame oil.Add some seasoning sauce, hot pepper paste and toasted sesame oil according to your taste and mix them well with a spoon and eat.Storing and reheatingRefrigerate leftover vegetable rice promptly in a covered container and use it within 3 days. Reheat it in the microwave until hot throughout. To reheat it in a steamer, bring the water to a boil, then put the rice in the steamer basket. Cover and steam for about 5 minutes, until hot throughout. Steaming makes it taste like freshly cooked vegetable rice again!
